public_rationale: Concrete AI-related medical development plans existed, but the examined records do not supply a qualifying AI-company plan to cure a specified disease within five to ten years. That does not prove none existed. Later announcements cannot contradict an assertion about what had already been presented by August 17.
limitations: The result is sensitive to the undefined meanings of 'AI company', 'real plan' and 'cure'.
Marcus's personal knowledge cannot be independently established.
The evidence review cannot prove an unrestricted historical negative.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As far as Marcus knows, no AI company has presented a real plan for curing even one disease in 5-10 years.

statement.excerpt: (As far as I know, the correct answer to the question about real plans posed in the first sentence is a simple “no”.)
statement.document_title: No, Dario Amodei, we will not be curing cancer and “most human disease” in five to ten years

from_speaker: cure even one disease in 5-10 years
our_interpretation: Assess the qualified public-record assertion, not Marcus's private knowledge.
The question covers plans publicly presented at any time up to August 17, 2026; 'ever' supplies no lower date bound.
A real plan identifies a disease, a proposed curative approach, development and clinical-testing steps, and an intended five-to-ten-year delivery timetable.
A plan need not already have succeeded or guarantee success.
AI companies includes specialist companies whose core business is AI-driven drug discovery.
A treatment program does not automatically constitute a cure plan.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive review of relevant public company disclosures establishes that none presented a plan meeting the disease, cure, development-path and timetable criteria by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one qualifying AI company publicly presented such a plan by August 17, 2026.

evidence.explanation: The announcement supplies a specific disease, AI-designed drug and concrete clinical trial. It does not present a five-to-ten-year cure-delivery commitment, so it is a near-counterexample rather than decisive contradiction.
The release presents an AI-enabled initiative aimed at an ALS cure. Its sponsor is a disease-focused nonprofit, so it does not establish the required AI-company counterexample.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated pre-August 17 company disclosure naming the disease, curative approach, development steps and five-to-ten-year timetable would contradict the assertion. Support would require a substantially more comprehensive review of relevant companies' public plans.
